svg.title: One file, two rooms for a Databricks project environment
svg.desc: Notebooks in a bundle share one serverless process in the editor. A scheduled job reads the same pyproject.toml through project_environment and runs each task in an isolated environment. The 22 October notes call both Betas. The Jobs API reference does not list the field.

g.text: 22 October notes: Beta. Off until an admin enables the preview.
Project-Scoped Shared Compute. AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud product notes.
One switch covers the bundle editor and the job file. It is not on by default.
Git Folders were already Beta on 2 September. That note does not mention the switch.
AWS and Google Cloud October headers still say 1 October. Serverless notes skip the line.
Editor room: one process
Notebooks and files in one bundle, or one
Git folder, share serverless compute.
Root pyproject.toml is optional.
When present, it replaces the side pane.
Editor example pins environment version 5.
%uv add updates the file, the lock, and
the environment. A direct edit needs sync.
Python names stay inside one notebook.
The first user to attach owns the run.
A second usage policy gets a second process.
A web terminal sits on the same resource.
Job room: the file only
Schedule copies the root file into the job
when the file exists. The process stays.
project_environment is the only source
field in spec. CLI 1.21.0 or above.
Job example pins environment version 6.
Requirements say 5 and above for both.
Version 5 is Connect 18. Version 6 is 19.
A stale uv.lock skips the lock and skips
installing the project package.
Each task keeps an isolated environment.
Wheel tasks need an absolute path.
The notes, the feature page, and the API do not share a scope.
October notes: notebook tasks and Python script tasks. Feature pages add Python wheel tasks.
A relative project_environment path is the Python file example. Wheel tasks refuse it.
Jobs API reference: environment_version or base_environment is required. No project_environment field.
dbt steps and JAR steps do not offer Environment source Project. Pipelines stay on the 11 September page.
That page still uses an editable install, and it tells pipelines to list dependencies in pipeline.yml.
Serverless notes on AWS and Google Cloud, header 22 October: newest entry is the 23 October cache preview.
Azure serverless notes match that shape. A notebook or job may land on aarch64 or x86_64.
Hatchling plus a current uv.lock installs the project. %uv lock --check is the page's comparison.
No compliance exclusion, government-cloud line, or separate meter on these pages. Rollout can take a week.
